AI search optimization vs. SEO vs. AEO vs. GEO
In this guide, we use “AI search optimization” as the big-picture term for getting your brand into AI answers. Here’s how it compares with SEO, AEO, and GEO:
Rank higher in traditional search results and earn clicks
Make content easy for answer engines to pull into direct answers
Improve visibility inside generative AI responses
On paper, SEO and AI search optimization look like separate jobs. In practice, they’re pretty tangled up.

As Logan Freedman, Global Head of SEO and AI Search at Manychat, puts it, “AI search optimization is the final form of SEO, not a replacement for it. You still need the fundamentals, because if a crawler can’t read your site, no model will cite it.”
So if you’ve already put work into SEO, good news: none of it goes to waste. But optimizing for AI search means thinking bigger than your website. (More on that below.)
Why does AI search optimization matter for marketers?

AI search optimization matters because AI is changing how people find and compare brands. They can ask an AI chatbot what to buy, which brands to consider, or what a product costs. If your brand isn’t part of the answer, it quietly drops out of the decision.
1. Brand visibility is bigger than your website
AI tools piece together their answers from all corners of the web.

To see this for yourself, Freedman has a simple exercise: Run a “best tool for X” prompt through ChatGPT or Perplexity, then look at the citations. Odds are, you’ll see Reddit threads, review sites, and YouTube videos.
“The brand’s own page is rarely the source. That tells you the signal is your whole company, not just your site,” he says.
The brands that win will be products people genuinely talk about, backed by marketing that’s firing on every channel at once.
2. Traditional website traffic is under pressure
AI Overviews are taking a big bite out of website traffic. And it makes sense: if the answer is sitting right at the top of the results page, there’s less reason to keep scrolling.

In a 2026 study of 300,000 Google search terms, Ahrefs found that when an AI Overview appeared at the top of the page, the top-ranking website had a 58% lower click-through rate than it would have without one.
Getting the top spot on Google is still important, but you also need to consider how to show up in AI-generated answers.
3. People are already turning to AI for research
Traditional search engines still lead when it comes to research, but AI is gaining ground.

Almost 25% of customers cite AI-powered platforms as their top research tool, according to Adobe’s 2026 AI and Digital Trends report. That’s a quarter of your potential customers who could be sizing up your brand inside a chat window.
How do AI search tools decide what to cite?
AI search tools don’t publish exactly how they choose sources. But generally, they’re more likely to cite content that’s relevant, credible, and original, on pages they can find and read.
Here are five qualities that make content useful to AI search tools:
Relevance: The content directly answers the person’s question.
Originality: It offers something new, like firsthand experience or original research.
Credibility: The content comes from a reputable source, and its claims are backed by evidence (think: named sources, experts, or data).
Depth: The topic is covered thoroughly. Completeness is the goal, not length.
Freshness: The information is accurate and up to date.
AI tools also need to be able to find, access, and make sense of your content. Here’s what matters on the technical side:
Crawlability: Your page is open to AI crawlers.
Page structure: Your content is organized with clear headings and logical sections.
Content accessibility: Important information is available as readable text, not stuck in images or JavaScript.
Indexability: Your page can be added to search engine indexes, making it easier for AI tools to find.
How do you optimize your content for AI search?
To optimize your content for AI search, focus on answering questions directly and backing them up with credible, original information. Then make sure AI tools can actually find and read your pages.
Answer the question directly, then add depth
Structure pages with clear headings, lists, and tables
Back claims with named, linked sources
Add original data and expert quotes
Use schema markup and keep pages crawlable
Build a list of the questions your customers would actually ask. Most fall into a few buckets:
Comparisons: “What’s the best X for Y?”
Decisions: “Should I use X or Z?”
Tradeoffs: “What are the drawbacks of X?”
Specific situations: “What’s best for a small team with a limited budget?”
Sales calls, support tickets, Reddit threads, and social mentions are all good places to look.
2. Answer the question directly, then add depth
Lead each section with the answer, then add the details later. Clear, direct answers make your content easier for AI search tools to interpret and reference.
For example, if a heading asks, “How much does X cost?” give the price first. Then explain plans, exceptions, or anything else people need to know.
3. Structure pages with clear headings, lists, and tables
Clear structure helps AI tools figure out what each part of a page is about, which makes it easier to pull out the right answer.
Start with your headings. Write them the way people actually ask questions, like “Is X worth it for small teams?” Then break up your content with:
Bullet points for options or features
Bonus: These tactics make your content easier for human readers to skim, too.
4. Back claims with named, linked sources
When you share a stat or make a claim, name the source and link to it. Clear sourcing shows your content is grounded in something real, which makes your page a safer bet for AI tools to cite.
5. Add original data and expert quotes

If your page says the same thing as 50 others, AI has no particular reason to pick yours. So give it something it can’t replicate, like original research, survey results, firsthand testing, or quotes from people with relevant expertise.
You don’t need a massive research budget, either. Even a small experiment or a genuinely useful observation adds something new to the conversation.
6. Use schema markup and keep pages crawlable

Don’t neglect technical SEO. Check that your pages can be crawled and indexed, and that key information doesn’t live inside images or JavaScript. If AI tools can’t read a page, it doesn’t matter how good the content is.
Next, consider adding schema markup. It’s a type of code that helps search engines interpret what’s on your page, including details like the author or publication date.
Schema markup doesn’t guarantee AI citations, but it does give search engines more context about your content.

AI tools want to give people current answers, so they tend to lean on current sources. A 2026 study by Seer Interactive found that 75% of pages cited by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity had been updated within the past year.
Freshness matters for accuracy, too. An AI tool might not realize your 2023 pricing page is out of date. It’ll just repeat whatever it finds, so make a habit of reviewing your most important pages.
How do brand mentions and social content affect AI search visibility?
AI search tools regularly pull from social platforms. That makes social content, especially what your customers and fans post, a big part of how AI search sees you.
Social posts can be cited directly in AI answers

Social content can show up as sources in AI answers, and it happens more than you might think. For example, ChatGPT cites LinkedIn in 4.9% of answers, according to a 2026 Searchable study. On Perplexity, that number jumps to 10.9%.
Brand mentions can shape how AI talks about your brand

Your website tells AI what you want people to think. Social media gives it a window into what people actually think. And, says Freedman, “That off-site chatter usually carries more weight than anything on your own domain.”
For example, when I asked ChatGPT if people like Facetune as an editing app, it came back with a list of pros and cons, with links to the Reddit threads behind them.
So if you’re wondering what AI thinks of your brand, start by checking what your customers are saying.

How do you measure AI search visibility?

You can measure AI search visibility by looking at first-party search reports, running monthly prompt tests, and tracking referral traffic. No single tool shows the full picture yet, so it helps to look at them together.
First-party search reports come straight from the search engines themselves. That makes them one of the most reliable ways to see how your website performs, including in AI-powered search.
Start with two free tools you may already use:
Google Search Console: See how your pages perform in Google Search, including traffic from AI Overviews and AI Mode.
Bing Webmaster Tools: Track how often your pages get cited in Microsoft Copilot and Bing’s AI answers, plus which pages are getting the most citations.
That gives you a useful baseline, but it’s only part of the picture.
2. Test the same prompts each month
Write down 20–50 questions your potential customers might ask AI, then test the questions on different AI tools, like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.
Mentions: Did AI mention your brand?
Recommendations: Did AI actually recommend it?
Position: Was your brand the first recommendation or further down?
Citations: Did AI link to your website?
Competitors: Did competing brands also appear?
You can track this in a simple spreadsheet. Repeat the process each month to see how your visibility changes.
3. Check referral traffic and business results
Showing up in AI search is great. But is it actually bringing people to your website?
In Google Analytics, look for referral traffic from AI tools like chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, and gemini.google.com. Look at which pages visitors land on and whether they take action.
Just remember: Not every AI search will lead to a click. Someone might stumble on your brand in an AI-generated answer and visit your website later through a different channel.
What mistakes hurt AI search visibility?
Some of the biggest AI search optimization mistakes come down to one thing: looking for a shortcut.
If that sounds familiar, it should. According to Freedman, it’s “the same thing that’s plagued SEO for a decade: chasing hacks.”
Right now, the hacks he sees most often include:
Buying your way onto “best of” listicles
Adding an llms.txt file (a text file that summarizes your site for AI tools) and calling it a strategy
These tactics may give you a bump in the short term. But AI models change fast, and what worked last month can stop working tomorrow.

For example, Freedman points to recent data from Peec AI, which found that the share of ChatGPT citations going to listicles fell by half after the GPT-5.6 update. “You put all that effort into spiking AI visibility and it falls off just as fast, exactly like Google,” he says.

What actually works is slower and a lot less flashy. “Visibility in AI search compounds slowly: real product, real customers talking about you, consistent coverage you earned,” Freedman observes. “Get-rich-quick doesn’t work here either.”

Is AI search optimization different from SEO?

AI search optimization builds on traditional SEO rather than replacing it. Traditional SEO focuses on improving rankings in search results, while AI search optimization focuses on getting your brand mentioned or cited in AI-generated answers. Many of the same tactics still apply, including earning backlinks and following Google’s E-E-A-T guidelines.
Does social media affect AI search visibility?

Yes. AI search tools can surface information from platforms like Reddit, LinkedIn, and Quora. Reviews, discussions, and firsthand experiences may shape how your brand is represented in AI-generated answers. Social content can also appear as a cited source in answers from AI platforms.
Can I see what AI says about my brand?

Yes. You can manually search for your brand across tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. You can also use AI visibility tools, like Lumen, to track brand mentions and sentiment over time. Just remember that answers can vary between tools and even between searches. Large language models don’t always give the same response to the same question.
What should marketers prioritize for AI search optimization?

Start with useful content that directly answers your audience’s questions. Then optimize your website for AI search by making sure important pages are crawlable, well-organized, and easy to read. That includes checking your robots.txt file and using structured data where it makes sense. And don’t forget to keep your content accurate. AI tools can retrieve fresh information, even though some of their underlying knowledge comes from older training data.
